cells.verb: feeling the full weight of something you pictured coming true
cells.place: at the finish of a thing that doubles as a doorway
cells.ask: Let what this made you feel choose the next direction — move toward whatever you were most alive while making, and start before the glow fades.
cells.core: Something you once only imagined is here now, and you're actually letting yourself feel it. Not checking it against the picture in your head, not already hunting for the flaw — just standing in it, full. That kind of satisfaction at a finish doesn't shut the door behind you; it's the thing that makes walking through the next one easy. If you want somewhere to spend it, let the feeling do the steering: notice what part of this you were most alive for, and go toward more of that while it's still warm.
cells.sheetLine: You dreamed it, it landed, and you're letting yourself feel it.

cells.tense: Future — tasting a finish that hasn't finished yet.
cells.verb: savoring the arrival ahead of the arriving
cells.place: at the finish of a thing that doubles as a doorway
cells.ask: Tend the thing as it actually is today — one plain, practical act of care, with no requirement that it feel like anything — and let dreaming come back later, from what you've actually lived through.
cells.core: You're already standing in how good it's going to feel. The thing isn't done, or it's done and not quite the way you pictured, and you're filling the gap with the satisfaction you were promised — so every look at the real work is a little bit a disappointment, and you keep looking anyway. Feeding on the finish before it's cooked leaves you hungry at the table. What might help is smaller than it sounds: give the thing as it stands one piece of honest care today, the kind you'd give a plant, without asking it to glow back. Dreams land better when they're grown from what you've actually been through.
cells.sheetLine: You're living in how it'll feel instead of in what it is.

cells.tense: Past — standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: finishing something without ever letting it land
cells.place: at the finish of a thing that doubles as a doorway
cells.ask: Before you decide what it was worth, hold still with one plain thing you know is true about what you made — no verdict, no feeling required — and let that knowing do the opening.
cells.core: You pictured it, you made it, and then nothing — the satisfaction that should have arrived at the finish didn't, or you didn't let it in, and you walked on with the door still open behind you. So the next thing you try to imagine comes up thin, because it's built on a finish you never fully stood in. Pushing yourself to feel proud now won't do it; that current doesn't start from feeling. It starts from knowing. Sit with the thing you finished and name, just to yourself, one true thing about it — not good, not bad, just true — and stay there without needing to conclude. Dreaming comes back when what you've lived through has actually been taken in.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it. You never let yourself arrive.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: being deeply satisfied by something you imagined into being
cells.place: at the finish of a thing that doubles as a doorway
cells.ask: Sort it carefully: pick one piece of what's here that you pictured before it existed, and say "I imagined that" — so the next dream can come from someone who knows it was theirs.
cells.core: You're content, and something you once only pictured is the reason — but ask you and you'd say it just worked out, timing, luck, other people. The satisfaction is real and it's running; the credit for it is being handed to the weather. That's how a finish fails to open: you can't walk through a door you don't believe you built. The repair is a matter of looking closely. Take the thing apart in your mind and separate what simply happened from what you saw first and then made happen. Find one piece in the second pile and claim it, plainly. Dreams that know where they came from are the ones that keep coming.
cells.sheetLine: It's what you imagined, and you're still calling it luck.
